beats: Hook: two players can't talk; each gets a random bit from the referee and answers with a bit; the best plan made in advance wins 3 rounds in 4; share one entangled pair beforehand and they win about 85%, yet they still can't send each other a single bit (line_qc_spooky_booths). The shared pair is drawn as two identical devices (two buttons, one small window): a result appears only when a button is pressed (a measurement), never as a coin already waiting in a box. Cast as in QC04-01 plus the referee.

Alice in California, Bob in New York, sharing a Bell pair (her framing, 64:53-65:44): line_qc_spooky_far_apart (a sunny beach vs. a snowy street: no maps, no flags, no landmarks). Alice presses and sees 0; Bob's result is then 0 too, however far apart.

Einstein's objection (her clip 74:07-74:33, "Einstein's pitfall"): faster than light? "Spooky action at a distance" is his phrase: quote it as his, never as a caption that claims physics; never draw him. Her lines only from the student dialogue 71:25-75:28.

Why it is not a telephone (her clip 65:44-66:37): Bob alone sees a fair 50/50 whether or not Alice pressed first (line_qc_spooky_bob_alone: two equal heaps); the match shows only when they compare notes, which needs an ordinary channel no faster than light (line_qc_spooky_compare_strips; reuse line_dials_daily_letter for the slow letter). Title beat: line_qc_spooky_tin_cans (the string is cut).

What it is not: a pair of gloves packed into two boxes also matches every time (line_qc_spooky_glove_boxes), and answers fixed in advance like that are exactly the 75% plan; Bell's point is that a game can tell the two apart.

The CHSH game (Q24-02 p37, tape it): the referee flips two coins x, y; Alice answers a, Bob answers b; they win if a XOR b = x AND y; any plan made in advance (line_qc_spooky_huddle; gloves included) wins at most 3/4; with a shared pair, each picks a button by their own coin and they win cos^2(pi/8), about 85.4% (Tsirelson).

Real experiments, a Nobel prize (her clip 75:54-76:50; she calls the game "gambling": keep or trim): Bell tests with entangled photons (2022 Nobel Prize in Physics: Aspect, Clauser, Zeilinger); line_qc_spooky_bell_table, a generic optics table: no named lab, no country, no race framing.

What a shared pair does buy (Q24-02 p35: the slide figure is from Wikipedia, redraw it): superdense coding, one qubit sent carries two classical bits (Bennett & Wiesner 1992): line_qc_spooky_dense_post (Alice turns her device to one of four settings and posts it; Bob reads one of four lamps). Teleportation is its mirror image (QC06-03).
Takeaway: correlation, not communication; the pair is a resource, not a wire. Reuse line_qc_tensor_carved_rings for the Bell pair when QC04-03 has been seen.
Cover (line_qc_cover_04_04; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the tinkerer on a beach and the friend in the snow hold tin cans to their ears; the string between them is cut.
